parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two parallel plates are 0.50 m apart and have potentials +200 V and +450 V. Determine the magnitude and direction of the uniform electric field between them.

answer.text: E = ΔV/d = 250/0.50 = 500 N C⁻¹, directed from the +450 V plate towards the +200 V plate.

bridge_result.text: The uniform electric field has magnitude 1.5 × 10³ N C⁻¹, directed from the positive plate to the negative plate.
bridge_result.origin: Earlier result supplied so you can start with this topic.

parts.label: whole
parts.given_text: The potential difference between the plates is K/q. Use this directly to find the uniform field strength.

parts.label: whole
parts.given_text: The potential difference between X and Y is K/e. Use this directly to find the uniform field strength.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Three paths lie in the plane of the page around isolated point charges. I is a circle centred on a positive charge. II is a non-circular ellipse centred on a positive charge. III is a circle centred on a negative charge. Which paths are equipotential?

A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

answer.text: B. For an isolated point charge V=kQ/r. Constant potential requires constant distance r from the charge, irrespective of its sign. Hence I and III are equipotential.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which sketch represents equipotential surfaces from three positive and one negative point charge?

A. Sketch A
B. Sketch B
C. Sketch C
D. Sketch D

answer.text: D. Three nearby like charges share enclosing equipotential regions, while the oppositely signed charge has a separated region. D has a group of three and an isolated fourth charge.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of magnitude 1.2 kV, gaining kinetic energy. Use e=1.602×10⁻¹⁹ C, mp=1.673×10⁻²⁷ kg and Eₖ=½mv². Calculate its final speed, neglecting relativistic effects.

answer.text: The electric field does work eV=1.602×10⁻¹⁹×1200=1.9224×10⁻¹⁶ J. This becomes kinetic energy, so v=√(2eV/mp)=4.79×10⁵ m s⁻¹, about 5×10⁵ m s⁻¹.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
The diagram shows equipotential lines with values in volts. Compare the electric fields at A and B on the horizontal dashed line.

A. E_A < E_B, in the same direction
B. E_A < E_B, in opposite directions
C. E_A > E_B, in the same direction
D. E_A > E_B, in opposite directions

answer.text: C. Equal 10 V intervals are more closely spaced at A, so the field there is stronger. Potential increases to the right at both points, so both fields point left.

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An isolated conducting sphere in vacuum carries charge +83 pC. Its surface electric potential is +1.2 V relative to infinity. Determine its radius using k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two large parallel conducting plates in vacuum are separated by d. One is at potential +V and the other at zero. Neglect edge effects. Sketch electric potential against distance x from the positive plate, for 0 ≤ x ≤ d.

answer.text: Draw a straight line from (0,V) to (d,0): potential is V(x) = V(1 − x/d). Its constant negative gradient corresponds to a uniform field directed from the positive plate towards the zero-potential plate.
